Matrix statistics: autonomy and eigenvalue distribution

Source: R/statistics.R
matrix_statistics.Rd

  • autonomy(): autonomy of a covariance matrix in the direction(s) beta (Hansen & Houle 2008), a(beta) = 1 / ((beta' G^-1 beta) (beta' G beta)) for unit vectors beta: the fraction of the variation in direction beta that is independent of other directions (1 when beta is an eigenvector).

  • mean_autonomy(): mean autonomy over n random directions.

  • eigen_variance(): proportion of the total variance on each principal component.

Usage

autonomy(m, beta)

mean_autonomy(m, n = 1000)

eigen_variance(m)

Arguments

m

a covariance matrix (e.g. a G or P matrix).

beta

a direction (vector) or several directions (columns of a matrix); normalised to unit length.

n

number of random directions.

Value

autonomy(): one value per direction. mean_autonomy(): a number. eigen_variance(): a vector of proportions in decreasing order.

Examples

G <- matrix(c(1, 0.8, 0.1, 0.8, 1, 0.1, 0.1, 0.1, 1), 3)
autonomy(G, c(1, 1, 0))
#> [1] 0.9888889
mean_autonomy(G)
#> [1] 0.637667
eigen_variance(G)
#> [1] 0.60808802 0.32524531 0.06666667
